name: Visual learning aids
summary: Where diagrams and field photos come from, what they are allowed to teach, and why they are not Evidence — Learner Mode's visual pillar, not a media CMS.
what_is_it: Berry agronomy is easier to learn with a labeled diagram (cane years, bed cross-section, trellis) or a rights-clear extension photograph (symptom, fruit stage, structure). Those assets live at the publisher: land-grant PDFs, USDA galleries, or other named public pages. Learner Mode may *link* to them. It does not scrape, host, or treat an image as a Fact, Signal, or Assessment. A picture of a disease is not a diagnosis of a competitor's field.
why_it_matters: Without a sourcing rule, it is tempting to paste unlabeled web images into teaching pages or to imply that a photo proves a company's practice. The visual pillar exists so diagrams have provenance and so teaching never masquerades as captured intelligence.
how_evaluated: A teaching visual is usable when the publisher is named, the URL is the public page or document, and the license or public-education reuse is clear enough to link. It is not evaluated by aesthetic quality or by whether it would look good on a Landscape slide.
what_affects_it: Copyright, publisher takedowns, and whether the image actually depicts the crop and structure named. Stock photos of 'berries' and unmarked social posts are not teaching aids here.
how_to_interpret: Links on this page and `media` entries on other concepts are educational citations, never Evidence. Do not promote a diagram into trusted data. If a source photo is later used in a publication draft, it still goes through Publication Review like any other item — Learner Mode is not a shortcut.
